message.content:
Lions (Panthera leo) belong to the family **Felidae** (order Carnivora), while zebras (Equus quagga) belong to the family **Equidae** (order Perissodactyla).  
Their most recent common ancestor is therefore the last common ancestor of the clade that contains both the orders Carnivora and Perissodactyla – essentially the last common ancestor of the super‑clade **Laurasiatheria**.  

This ancestor would have been a small, probably insectivorous mammal that lived roughly **70–80 million years ago** (late Cretaceous). In a broader sense, the last common ancestor of all placental mammals (which includes both lineages) lived about **160 million years ago**.
